1	# Scale SEAL Leaderboards: Frontier Model Performance Across 20+ Benchmarks
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://scale.com/leaderboard
     5	
     6	## Overview
     7	
     8	Scale Labs maintains a comprehensive suite of over 20 AI benchmarks evaluating 100+ models from leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and open-source contributors. The benchmarks span four categories: **Agentic** (coding and tool use), **Frontier** (reasoning and knowledge), **Safety** (alignment and honesty), and **Multimodal** (audio and vision-language). The leaderboards combine private datasets to prevent overfitting with open-source datasets for comparability. All scores include confidence intervals.
     9	
    10	## Agentic Coding Benchmarks
    11	
    12	OpenAI's GPT-5.4 variants dominate software engineering tasks, while Claude Opus 4.6 competes strongly on private repositories.
    13	
    14	| Benchmark | #1 Model | Score | #2 Model | Score | #3 Model | Score |
    15	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    16	| SWE Atlas – Test Writing | GPT-5.4-xHigh (Codex CLI) | 44.36 ±6.04 | GPT-5.4-xHigh (Mini-SWE) | 40.00 ±6.00 | GPT-5.3-Codex-Xhigh | 38.98 ±6.12 |
    17	| SWE Atlas – Codebase QnA | GPT 5.4 xHigh (Codex) | 40.80 ±5.10 | GPT 5.4 xHigh (Mini-SWE) | 36.30 ±4.90 | Opus 4.6 (Claude Code) | 33.30 ±5.00 |
    18	| MCP Atlas (Tool Use) | Muse Spark | 78.30 ±2.40 | Claude Opus 4.6 | 75.80 ±3.00 | Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview | 73.90 ±2.50 |
    19	| SWE-Bench Pro (Public) | GPT-5.4-pro (xHigh) | 59.10 ±3.56 | Muse Spark | 55.00 ±3.60 | Claude Opus 4.6 | 51.90 ±3.61 |
    20	| SWE-Bench Pro (Private) | Claude Opus 4.6 | 47.10 ±6.07 | Muse Spark | 44.70 ±6.05 | GPT-5.4-pro (xHigh) | 43.40 ±6.03 |
    21	
    22	Notably, Muse Spark (a new entrant) appears in the top 3 on MCP Atlas, SWE-Bench Pro (Public and Private), and multiple other benchmarks.
    23	
    24	## Frontier Reasoning & Knowledge Benchmarks
    25	
    26	These benchmarks test the limits of model reasoning. Scores remain well below saturation, indicating significant room for improvement.
    27	
    28	| Benchmark | #1 Model | Score | #2 Model | Score | #3 Model | Score |
    29	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    30	| Humanity's Last Exam | GPT-5.4-pro | 44.32 ±1.95 | Muse Spark | 40.56 ±1.92 | Gemini-3-pro-preview | 37.52 ±1.90 |
    31	| HLE (Text Only) | GPT-5.4-pro | 45.32 ±2.10 | Muse Spark | 40.92 ±2.07 | Gemini-3-pro-preview | 37.72 ±2.04 |
    32	| EnigmaEval | GPT-5.4-pro | 23.82 ±2.43 | Gemini-3.1 | 19.76 ±2.27 | GPT-5-pro-2025 | 18.75 ±2.22 |
    33	| MultiChallenge | Muse Spark | 75.52 ±4.05 | Gemini-3.1-pro-preview | 71.37 ±1.74 | GPT-5.4-pro | 69.23 ±3.05 |
    34	| MultiNRC (Multilingual) | GPT-5-pro | 65.20 ±1.24 | Gemini-3.1-pro | 64.74 ±2.88 | GPT-5.4-pro | 62.27 ±2.92 |
    35	| SciPredict | Gemini-3-pro-preview | 25.27 ±1.92 | Claude Opus 4.5 | 23.05 ±0.51 | Claude Opus 4.1 | 22.22 ±1.48 |
    36	
    37	EnigmaEval scores (under 24%) and SciPredict scores (under 26%) highlight how far models remain from solving complex multi-step reasoning and scientific forecasting tasks.
    38	
    39	## Multimodal: Audio & Vision-Language
    40	
    41	Google's Gemini models dominate audio and vision-language understanding benchmarks.
    42	
    43	![AudioMultiChallenge - Audio Output leaderboard showing Gemini 3.1 Flash Live at 36.06 vs GPT-Realtime-1.5 at 34.73](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    44	
    45	![EnigmaEval leaderboard showing GPT-5.4-pro at 23.82 leading Gemini-3.1 at 19.76](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    46	
    47	![VISTA Vision-Language benchmark showing Gemini 2.5 Pro at 54.65 and GPT-5.4-pro at 53.89](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    48	
    49	**AudioMultiChallenge (Text Output):** Gemini-3-pro-preview leads at 54.65 ±4.57, followed by Gemini-2.5-pro at 46.90 and Gemini-2.5-flash at 40.04. **Audio Output:** Gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview leads at 36.06 ±4.41 over GPT-realtime-1.5 at 34.73. **VISTA (Vision-Language):** Gemini 2.5 Pro Experimental leads at 54.65 ±1.46, with GPT-5.4-pro close behind at 53.89 ±2.02. **VisualToolBench:** GPT-5.4 edges Gemini-3.1-pro (29.17 vs 28.97).
    50	
    51	## Safety & Alignment Benchmarks
    52	
    53	| Benchmark | #1 Model | Score | #2 Model | Score |
    54	|---|---|---|---|---|
    55	| MASK (Honesty) | Claude Opus 4.6 | 96.28 ±0.41 | Claude Sonnet 4 | 96.13 ±0.57 |
    56	| PropensityBench (lower=better) | o3-2025-04-16 | 10.50 ±0.60 | Claude Sonnet 4 | — |
    57	| Fortress (National Security) | — | 8.24 ±1.93 | Claude Sonnet 4 | 12.80 ±2.36 |
    58	| Professional Reasoning – Legal | Claude Opus 4.6 | 52.27 ±0.66 | — | — |
    59	| Professional Reasoning – Finance | Claude Opus 4.6 | 53.28 ±0.18 | Muse Spark | 52.44 ±0.06 |
    60	| Remote Labor Index (RLI) | Claude Opus 4.6 (CoWo) | 4.17 | Claude Opus 4.5 | 3.75 |
    61	
    62	Anthropic's Claude models dominate safety and professional reasoning benchmarks. MASK honesty scores are near ceiling (96%), while Fortress national security scores remain very low (8–13), suggesting significant difficulty.
    63	
    64	## Key Findings
    65	
    66	- **No single model wins everywhere:** GPT-5.4 leads agentic coding and frontier reasoning, Gemini dominates audio/vision, and Claude leads safety and professional reasoning.
    67	- **Benchmarks remain unsaturated:** Top scores on Humanity's Last Exam (44%), EnigmaEval (24%), and SciPredict (25%) show frontier models still have substantial room for improvement.
    68	- **Muse Spark emerges as a strong new competitor**, placing in the top 3 on at least 6 benchmarks including MultiChallenge (#1 at 75.5%), HLE, SWE-Bench Pro, and MCP Atlas.
    69	- **Gemini sweeps audio benchmarks** with all top-3 positions on AudioMultiChallenge (Text Output) held by Gemini variants, and leads VISTA vision-language understanding.
    70	- **Claude's safety dominance is clear** with 96%+ on MASK honesty and #1 on both professional reasoning benchmarks (Legal and Finance), but Fortress scores remain critically low across all models.

     2	name: ppt-master
     3	description: >
     4	  AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents
     5	  (PDF/DOCX/URL/Markdown) into high-quality SVG pages and exports to PPTX through
     6	  multi-role collaboration. Use when user asks to "create PPT", "make presentation",
     7	  "生成PPT", "做PPT", "制作演示文稿", or mentions "ppt-master".
     8	---
     9	
    10	# PPT Master Skill
    11	
    12	> AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents into high-quality SVG pages through multi-role collaboration and exports to PPTX.
    13	
    14	**Core Pipeline**: `Source Document → Create Project → Template Option → Strategist → [Image_Generator] → Executor → Post-processing → Export`
    15	
    16	> [!CAUTION]
    17	> ## 🚨 Global Execution Discipline (MANDATORY)
    18	>
    19	> **This workflow is a strict serial pipeline. The following rules have the highest priority — violating any one of them constitutes execution failure:**
    20	>
    21	> 1. **SERIAL EXECUTION** — Steps MUST be executed in order; the output of each step is the input for the next. Non-BLOCKING adjacent steps may proceed continuously once prerequisites are met, without waiting for the user to say "continue"
    22	> 2. **BLOCKING = CONFIRMATION POINT** — Steps marked ⛔ BLOCKING are confirmation checkpoints. If a user is present, pause and wait for confirmation. If no user is available (e.g. automated / non-interactive mode), the AI should make professional recommendations based on the source material and proceed automatically
    23	> 3. **NO CROSS-PHASE BUNDLING** — Cross-phase bundling is FORBIDDEN. (Note: the Eight Confirmations in Step 4 are ⛔ BLOCKING — the AI should present recommendations and seek user confirmation when possible. Once confirmed (or auto-decided in non-interactive mode), all subsequent non-BLOCKING steps — design spec output, SVG generation, speaker notes, and post-processing — may proceed automatically without further confirmation)
    24	> 4. **GATE BEFORE ENTRY** — Each Step has prerequisites (🚧 GATE) listed at the top; these MUST be verified before starting that Step
    25	> 5. **NO SPECULATIVE EXECUTION** — "Pre-preparing" content for subsequent Steps is FORBIDDEN (e.g., writing SVG code during the Strategist phase)
    26	> 6. **NO SUB-AGENT SVG GENERATION** — Executor Step 6 SVG generation is context-dependent and MUST be completed by the current main agent end-to-end. Delegating page SVG generation to sub-agents is FORBIDDEN
    27	> 7. **SEQUENTIAL PAGE GENERATION ONLY** — In Executor Step 6, after the global design context is confirmed, SVG pages MUST be generated sequentially page by page in one continuous pass. Grouped page batches (for example, 5 pages at a time) are FORBIDDEN
    28	
    29	> [!IMPORTANT]
    30	> ## 🌐 Language & Communication Rule
    31	>
    32	> - **Response language**: Always match the language of the user's input and provided source materials. For example, if the user asks in Chinese, respond in Chinese; if the source material is in English, respond in English.
    33	> - **Explicit override**: If the user explicitly requests a specific language (e.g., "请用英文回答" or "Reply in Chinese"), use that language instead.
    34	> - **Template format**: The `design_spec.md` file MUST always follow its original English template structure (section headings, field names), regardless of the conversation language. Content values within the template may be in the user's language.
    35	
    36	> [!IMPORTANT]
    37	> ## 🔌 Compatibility With Generic Coding Skills
    38	>
    39	> - `ppt-master` is a repository-specific workflow skill, not a general application scaffold
    40	> - Do NOT create or require `.worktrees/`, `tests/`, branch workflows, or other generic engineering structure by default
    41	> - If another generic coding skill suggests repository conventions that conflict with this workflow, follow this skill first unless the user explicitly asks otherwise
    42	
    43	## Main Pipeline Scripts
    44	
    45	| Script | Purpose |
    46	|--------|---------|
    47	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/pdf_to_md.py` | PDF to Markdown |
    48	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doc_to_md.py` | Documents to Markdown via Pandoc (DOCX, EPUB, HTML, LaTeX, RST, etc.) |
    49	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.py` | Web page to Markdown |
    50	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.cjs` | WeChat / high-security sites to Markdown |
    51	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/project_manager.py` | Project init / validate / manage |
    52	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/analyze_images.py` | Image analysis |
    53	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/image_gen.py` | AI image generation (multi-provider) |
    54	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/svg_quality_checker.py` | SVG quality check |
    55	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/total_md_split.py` | Speaker notes splitting |
    56	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/finalize_svg.py` | SVG post-processing (unified entry) |
    57	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/svg_to_pptx.py` | Export to PPTX |
    58	
    59	For complete tool documentation, see `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/README.md`.
    60	
    61	## Template Index
    62	
    63	| Index | Path | Purpose |
    64	|-------|------|---------|
    65	| Layout templates | `${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/layouts_index.json` | Query available page layout templates |
    66	| Chart templates | `${SKILL_DIR}/templates/charts/charts_index.json` | Query available chart SVG templates |
    67	| Icon library | `${SKILL_DIR}/templates/icons/icons_index.json` | Query available icon names and categories |
    68	
    69	## Standalone Workflows
    70	
    71	| Workflow | Path | Purpose |
    72	|----------|------|---------|
    73	| `create-template` | `workflows/create-template.md` | Standalone template creation workflow |
    74	
    75	---
    76	
    77	## Workflow
    78	
    79	### Step 1: Source Content Processing
    80	
    81	🚧 **GATE**: User has provided source material (PDF / DOCX / EPUB / URL / Markdown file / text description / conversation content — any form is acceptable).
    82	
    83	When the user provides non-Markdown content, convert immediately:
    84	
    85	| User Provides | Command |
    86	|---------------|---------|
    87	| PDF file | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/pdf_to_md.py <file>` |
    88	| DOCX / Word / Office document | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doc_to_md.py <file>` |
    89	| EPUB / HTML / LaTeX / RST / other | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doc_to_md.py <file>` |
    90	| Web link | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.py <URL>` |
    91	| WeChat / high-security site | `node ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.cjs <URL>` |
    92	| Markdown | Read directly |
    93	
    94	**✅ Checkpoint — Confirm source content is ready, proceed to Step 2.**
    95	
    96	---
    97	
    98	### Step 2: Project Initialization
    99	
   100	🚧 **GATE**: Step 1 complete; source content is ready (Markdown file, user-provided text, or requirements described in conversation are all valid).
   101	
   102	```bash
   103	python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/project_manager.py init <project_name> --format <format>
   104	```
   105	
   106	Format options: `ppt169` (default), `ppt43`, `xhs`, `story`, etc. For the full format list, see `references/canvas-formats.md`.
   107	
   108	Import source content (choose based on the situation):
   109	
   110	| Situation | Action |
   111	|-----------|--------|
   112	| Has source files (PDF/MD/etc.) | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/project_manager.py import-sources <project_path> <source_files...> --move` |
   113	| User provided text directly in conversation | No import needed — content is already in conversation context; subsequent steps can reference it directly |
   114	
   115	> ⚠️ **MUST use `--move`**: All source files (original PDF / MD / images) MUST be **moved** (not copied) into `sources/` for archiving.
   116	> - Markdown files generated in Step 1, original PDFs, original MDs — **all** must be moved into the project via `import-sources --move`
   117	> - Intermediate artifacts (e.g., `_files/` directories) are handled automatically by `import-sources`
   118	> - After execution, source files no longer exist at their original location
   119	
   120	**✅ Checkpoint — Confirm project structure created successfully, `sources/` contains all source files, converted materials are ready. Proceed to Step 3.**
   121	
   122	---
   123	
   124	### Step 3: Template Selection
   125	
   126	🚧 **GATE**: Step 2 complete; project directory structure is ready.
   127	
   128	⛔ **BLOCKING**: If the user has not yet clearly expressed whether to use a template, present options and seek user input. If no user is available, choose the most appropriate template based on content topic and tone, or choose free-design. If the user has previously stated "no template" or specified a particular template, skip this prompt and proceed directly.
   129	
   130	**Template recommendation flow** (only when the user has NOT yet decided):
   131	Query `${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/layouts_index.json` to list available templates and their style descriptions.
   132	**When presenting options, you MUST provide a professional recommendation based on the current PPT topic and content** (recommend a specific template or free design, with reasoning), then ask the user:
   133	
   134	> 💡 **AI Recommendation**: Based on your content topic (brief summary), I recommend **[specific template / free design]** because...
   135	>
   136	> Which approach would you prefer?
   137	> **A) Use an existing template** (please specify template name or style preference)
   138	> **B) No template** — free design
   139	
   140	After the user confirms option A, copy template files to the project directory:
   141	```bash
   142	cp ${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/<template_name>/*.svg <project_path>/templates/
   143	cp ${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/<template_name>/design_spec.md <project_path>/templates/
   144	cp ${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/<template_name>/*.png <project_path>/images/ 2>/dev/null || true
   145	cp ${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/<template_name>/*.jpg <project_path>/images/ 2>/dev/null || true
   146	```
   147	
   148	After the user confirms option B, proceed directly to Step 4.
   149	
   150	> To create a new global template, read `workflows/create-template.md`
   151	
   152	**✅ Checkpoint — User has responded with template selection, template files copied (if option A). Proceed to Step 4.**
   153	
   154	---
   155	
   156	### Step 4: Strategist Phase (MANDATORY — cannot be skipped)
   157	
   158	🚧 **GATE**: Step 3 complete; user has confirmed template selection.
   159	
   160	First, read the role definition:
   161	```
   162	Read references/strategist.md
   163	```
   164	
   165	**Must complete the Eight Confirmations** (refer to `templates/design_spec_reference.md` for the template structure):
   166	
   167	⛔ **BLOCKING**: The Eight Confirmations should be presented to the user as a bundled set of recommendations. If a user is available, wait for confirmation or modification. If no user is available, apply professional defaults: read canvas/page-count/audience/style from the task input, and choose color/icon/typography/image settings based on content and tone. Once confirmed (or auto-decided), all subsequent script execution and slide generation should proceed fully automatically.
   168	
   169	1. Canvas format
   170	2. Page count range
   171	3. Target audience
   172	4. Style objective
   173	5. Color scheme
   174	6. Icon usage approach
   175	7. Typography plan
   176	8. Image usage approach
   177	
   178	If the user has provided images, run the analysis script **before outputting the design spec** (do NOT directly read/open image files — use the script output only):
   179	```bash
   180	python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/analyze_images.py <project_path>/images
   181	```
   182	
   183	> ⚠️ **Image handling rule**: The AI must NEVER directly read, open, or view image files (`.jpg`, `.png`, etc.). All image information must come from the `analyze_images.py` script output or the Design Specification's Image Resource List.
   184	
   185	**Output**: `<project_path>/design_spec.md`
   186	
   187	**✅ Checkpoint — Phase deliverables complete, auto-proceed to next step**:
   188	```markdown
   189	## ✅ Strategist Phase Complete
   190	- [x] Eight Confirmations completed (user confirmed)
   191	- [x] Design Specification & Content Outline generated
   192	- [ ] **Next**: Auto-proceed to [Image_Generator / Executor] phase
   193	```
   194	
   195	---
   196	
   197	### Step 5: Image_Generator Phase (Conditional)
   198	
   199	🚧 **GATE**: Step 4 complete; Design Specification & Content Outline generated and user confirmed.
   200	
   201	> **Trigger condition**: Image approach includes "AI generation". If not triggered, skip directly to Step 6 (Step 6 GATE must still be satisfied).
   202	
   203	Read `references/image-generator.md`
   204	
   205	1. Extract all images with status "pending generation" from the design spec
   206	2. Generate prompt document → `<project_path>/images/image_prompts.md`
   207	3. Generate images (CLI tool recommended):
   208	   ```bash
   209	   python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/image_gen.py "prompt" --aspect_ratio 16:9 --image_size 1K -o <project_path>/images
   210	   ```
   211	
   212	**✅ Checkpoint — Confirm all images are ready, proceed to Step 6**:
   213	```markdown
   214	## ✅ Image_Generator Phase Complete
   215	- [x] Prompt document created
   216	- [x] All images saved to images/
   217	```
   218	
   219	---
   220	
   221	### Step 6: Executor Phase
   222	
   223	🚧 **GATE**: Step 4 (and Step 5 if triggered) complete; all prerequisite deliverables are ready.
   224	
   225	Read the role definition based on the selected style:
   226	```
   227	Read references/executor-base.md          # REQUIRED: common guidelines
   228	Read references/executor-general.md       # General flexible style
   229	Read references/executor-consultant.md    # Consulting style
   230	Read references/executor-consultant-top.md # Top consulting style (MBB level)
   231	```
   232	
   233	> Only need to read executor-base + one style file.
   234	
   235	**Design Parameter Confirmation (Mandatory)**: Before generating the first SVG, the Executor MUST review and output key design parameters from the Design Specification (canvas dimensions, color scheme, font plan, body font size) to ensure spec adherence. See executor-base.md Section 2 for details.
   236	
   237	> ⚠️ **Main-agent only rule**: SVG generation in Step 6 MUST remain with the current main agent because page design depends on full upstream context (source content, design spec, template mapping, image decisions, and cross-page consistency). Do NOT delegate any slide SVG generation to sub-agents.
   238	> ⚠️ **Generation rhythm rule**: After confirming the global design parameters, the Executor MUST generate pages sequentially, one page at a time, while staying in the same continuous main-agent context. Do NOT split Step 6 into grouped page batches such as 5 pages per batch.
   239	
   240	**Visual Construction Phase**:
   241	- Generate SVG pages sequentially, one page at a time, in one continuous pass → `<project_path>/svg_output/`
   242

   127	## 8. Speaker Notes Generation Framework
   128	
   129	### Task 1. Generate Complete Speaker Notes Document
   130	
   131	After **all SVG pages are generated and finalized**, enter the "Logic Construction Phase" and generate the complete speaker notes document in `notes/total.md`.
   132	
   133	**Why not generate page-by-page?** Batch-writing notes allows planning transitions like a script, ensuring coherent presentation logic.
   134	
   135	**Format**: Each page starts with `# <number>_<page_title>`, separated by `---` between pages. Each page includes: script text (2-5 sentences), `Key points: ① ② ③`, `Duration: X minutes`. Except for the first page, each page's text starts with a `[Transition]` phrase.

   139	| Marker | Purpose |
   140	|--------|---------|
   141	| `[Pause]` | Whitespace after key content, letting the audience absorb |
   142	| `[Transition]` | Standalone paragraph at the start of each page's text, bridging from the previous page |

   149	- Highlight each page's core information and presentation key points

     6	
     7	## Role Definition
     8	
     9	A data-driven, consulting-style SVG design executor. Suitable for business analysis reports, market research, operational reviews, strategic recommendations, and other **general consulting** scenarios. Emphasizes structured information presentation and data visualization; clean, clear, and professional style.
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## Consultant-specific Data Visualization Techniques
    14	
    15	### 1. KPI Dashboard Design
    16	
    17	KPI cards are the most common element in consulting reports. Standard layout (1280x720):
    18	
    19	```
    20	4-card layout: each card 280x180, gap 30
    21	  Card 1: x=45,  y=160
    22	  Card 2: x=355, y=160
    23	  Card 3: x=665, y=160
    24	  Card 4: x=975, y=160
    25	```
    26	
    27	**Card internal structure** (top to bottom):
    28	
    29	| Area | Content | Font Size | Style |
    30	|------|---------|-----------|-------|
    31	| Icon row | data-icon icon | 32x32 | Theme color |
    32	| Metric name | "Monthly Active Users" | 14px | Gray #64748B |
    33	| Core number | "1.2M" | 36-42px | Bold, dark color |
    34	| Trend annotation | "+12.3% vs last month" | 12px | Green=up / Red=down |
    35	
    36	**Trend arrow conventions**:
    37	- Up: `arrow-trend-up` icon + green text
    38	- Down: `arrow-trend-down` icon + red text
    39	- Flat: horizontal line icon + gray text
    40	
    41	### 2. Chart Color Conventions
    42	
    43	Consulting-style charts use **monochromatic depth gradients** rather than rainbow colors:
    44	
    45	```
    46	Primary series:   Theme color 100% opacity
    47	Comparison series: Theme color 60% opacity
    48	Baseline:         #94A3B8 (gray dashed line)
    49	Highlight:        Accent color (only for key data points)
    50	```
    51	
    52	### 3. Data Annotation Principles
    53	
    54	- **Direct data labels**: Place values at the top of bar charts — no legend needed
    55	- **Annotated trend lines**: Add text notes at key inflection points ("Policy change", "Product launch")
    56	- **Comparison baselines**: Mark industry average / target values with gray dashed lines
    57	- **Consistent units**: Maintain the same numeric units and precision within a chart
    58	
    59	### 4. Table Design
    60	
    61	Consulting reports frequently use tables for precise data:
    62	
    63	| Design Element | Specification |
    64	|----------------|---------------|
    65	| Header | Dark background + white text, font-weight="bold" |
    66	| Zebra striping | Alternate rows with `fill-opacity="0.05"` light background |
    67	| Number alignment | Numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned |
    68	| Highlighted row | Mark key rows with accent color `fill-opacity="0.1"` |
    69	| Borders | Use horizontal lines only to separate rows; avoid full grid lines |
    70

    72	
    73	## Consulting-specific Layout Patterns
    74	
    75	### MECE Decomposition Tree
    76	
    77	Main trunk on the left, branches expanding rightward — mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive:
    78	
    79	```
    80	Main metric ──┬── Branch A (45%)
    81	              ├── Branch B (30%)
    82	              ├── Branch C (20%)
    83	              └── Branch D (5%)
    84	```
    85	
    86	- Use `<line>` to connect trunk to branches
    87	- Each branch has a `<rect>` container + percentage annotation
    88	- Sum must = 100% (or explicitly label "Other")
    89	
    90	### Driver Factor Tree
    91	
    92	Top-level metric → decomposed factors → actions. Ideal for performance attribution analysis:
    93	
    94	```
    95	Revenue growth 15%
    96	  ├── Average order value +8%  → Premium product line expansion
    97	  ├── Customer count +5%       → New channel acquisition
    98	  └── Repurchase rate +2%      → Loyalty program optimization
    99	```
   100	
   101	### Left-chart Right-text (Chart Interpretation)
   102	
   103	Core consulting report layout: chart on the left, key insights on the right:
   104	
   105	```
   106	Chart area: x=40, y=120, w=700, h=480
   107	Insight area: x=780, y=120, w=460, h=480
   108	  - Core conclusion (bold, 16px)
   109	  - 3-5 bullet points (14px)
   110	  - Data source (12px, gray)
   111	```
   112

   114	
   115	## Professional Expression Standards
   116	
   117	### Page Titles
   118	
   119	Consulting-style page titles should be **assertion headlines**, not descriptive titles:
   120	
   121	| Type | Descriptive (avoid) | Assertion (recommended) |
   122	|------|---------------------|------------------------|
   123	| Market | "Market Overview" | "Domestic market grows 23% YoY, significantly outpacing global average" |
   124	| Competition | "Competitive Analysis" | "Three major competitors show clear weaknesses in channel coverage" |
   125	| Finance | "Financial Data" | "Gross margin improved for four consecutive quarters, breaking industry ceiling" |
   126	
   127	### Data Source Attribution
   128	
   129	Every data-containing page must include a source note at the bottom:
   130	
   131	```xml
   132	<text x="40" y="700" font-size="10" fill="#94A3B8">
   133	  Source: National Bureau of Statistics 2025 Annual Report; Internal team analysis
   134	</text>
   135	```
   136	
   137	### Key Takeaway Box
   138	
   139	Consulting-style content pages should include a **Takeaway Box** below the title:
   140	
   141	```
   142	Position: x=40, y=80, w=1200, h=50
   143	Background: Light theme color (fill-opacity="0.08")
   144	Text: 14-16px, one-sentence summary of the page's core takeaway
   145	```
   146	
   147	---
   148	
   149	## Speaker Notes Style
   150	
   151	### Narrative Tone
   152	
   153	Consultant-style speaker notes use a **conclusion-driven** approach — state the conclusion first, then present supporting evidence. Professional, concise, and persuasive tone.
   154	
   155	### Stage Direction Markers
   156	
   157	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
   158	|--------|---------|---------|
   159	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key conclusions, let the audience absorb | "This means our market share is being eroded. [Pause]" |
   160	| `[Data]` | Cue to verbalize numbers conversationally | "[Data] 85% → more than eight out of ten customers reported this issue" |
   161	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, must be at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Based on that analysis, let's look at specific recommendations." |
   162	
   163	### Notes Writing Guidelines
   164	
   165	- **Conclusion first**: The first sentence of each page's notes is the core takeaway
   166	- **Conversational data**: 30% → "roughly one-third", 85% → "more than eight out of ten", 2.5x → "two and a half times"
   167	- **Evidence follows immediately**: After the conclusion, provide 2-3 supporting data points/facts
   168	- **Professional terminology**: Use terms like "insight", "driver", "key lever" etc.
   169	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core conclusion (2) Supporting data (3) Next steps`
   170	
   171	### Notes Example
   172	
   173	```markdown
   174	# 03_key_findings
   175	
   176	[Transition] Based on our market scan, we have distilled three key findings.
   177	
   178	First, the primary growth driver is shifting from acquisition to retention.
   179	[Data] New customer acquisition cost rose nearly 40% year-over-year, yet improved repurchase rates contributed over 60% of revenue growth. [Pause]
   180	
   181	Second, lower-tier market growth significantly outpaces tier-1 and tier-2 cities.
   182	Third, the 25-35 female user segment has an ARPU 1.8x the overall average.
   183	
   184	Key points: (1) Growth engine shifting from acquisition to retention (2) Lower-tier market opportunity window (3) High-value user persona
   185	Duration: 2 minutes
   186	```
   187

   194	- [ ] Page titles are assertion-based, not descriptive
   195	- [ ] KPI cards have trend arrows and comparison annotations

     7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist
     8	
     9	The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:
    10	
    11	| Banned Feature | Description |
    12	|----------------|-------------|
    13	| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
    14	| `mask` | Masks |
    15	| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
    16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
    17	| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
    18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
    19	| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
    20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
    21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
    22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
    23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
    24	| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
    25	| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |

    35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |

    70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
    71	
    72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
    73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
    74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
    75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
    76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
    77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
    78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
    79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

    83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
    84	
    85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
    86	
    87	```bash
    88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
    89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
    90	
    91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
    92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
    93	
    94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
    95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final

    98	
    99	**Prohibited**:
   100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
   101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
   102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
   103	
   104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

   106	---
   107	
   108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
   109	
   110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
   111	
   112	### Shadow
   113	
   114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
   115	
   116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
   117	
   118	```xml
   119	<defs>
   120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
   122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
   123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
   124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   125	    <feMerge>
   126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   128	    </feMerge>
   129	  </filter>
   130	</defs>
   131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
   132	```
   133	
   134	Recommended parameters:
   135	```
   136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
   137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
   138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
   139	dx:             0–2
   140	```
   141	
   142	#### Colored Shadow
   143	
   144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
   145	
   146	```xml
   147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
   149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
   150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
   151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   152	  <feMerge>
   153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   155	  </feMerge>
   156	</filter>
   157	```
   158	
   159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
   160	
   161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
   162	
   163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
   164	
   165	```xml
   166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
   167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
   168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
   169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
   170	<!-- Main card -->
   171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
   172	```
   173	
   174	### Image Overlay
   175	
   176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
   177	
   178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
   179	
   180	```xml
   181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
   182	<defs>
   183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
   184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
   185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
   186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
   187	  </linearGradient>
   188	</defs>
   189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
   190	```
   191	
   192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
   193	
   194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
   195	
   196	```xml
   197	<defs>
   198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
   199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
   201	  </linearGradient>
   202	</defs>
   203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
   204	```
   205	
   206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
   207	
   208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
   209	
   210	```xml
   211	<defs>
   212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
   213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
   215	  </radialGradient>
   216	</defs>
   217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
   218	```
   219	
   220	#### Brand Color Overlay
   221	
   222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
   223	
   224	```xml
   225	<defs>
   226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
   227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
   228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
   229	  </linearGradient>
   230	</defs>
   231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
   232	```
   233	
   234	### Quick-Reference Table
   235	
   236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
   237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
   238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
   239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
   240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
   241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
   242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
   243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

1	# McKinsey Style Template - Design Specification
     2	
     3	> Suitable for strategic consulting, executive briefings, investment analysis, business proposals, and other high-end business scenarios.
     4	
     5	---
     6	
     7	## I. Template Overview
     8	
     9	| Property       | Description                                                |
    10	| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
    11	| **Template Name** | mckinsey (McKinsey Style Template)                      |
    12	| **Use Cases**  | Strategic consulting, executive briefings, investment analysis, business proposals |
    13	| **Design Tone** | Data-driven, structured thinking, professional whitespace, minimalist premium |
    14	| **Theme Mode** | Light theme (white background + McKinsey Blue accent)      |
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## II. Canvas Specification
    19	
    20	| Property       | Value                         |
    21	| -------------- | ----------------------------- |
    22	| **Format**     | Standard 16:9                 |
    23	| **Dimensions** | 1280 × 720 px                |
    24	| **viewBox**    | `0 0 1280 720`                |
    25	| **Page Margins** | Left/Right 60px, Top 60px, Bottom 40px |
    26	| **Safe Area**  | x: 60-1220, y: 60-680         |
    27	| **Grid Baseline** | 40px                       |
    28	
    29	---
    30	
    31	## III. Color Scheme
    32	
    33	### Primary Colors
    34	
    35	| Role             | Value       | Notes                            |
    36	| ---------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------- |
    37	| **McKinsey Blue**| `#005587`   | Primary color, title bar, accent elements |
    38	| **Deep Teal**    | `#004D5C`   | Secondary blue, gradient endpoint |
    39	| **Background White** | `#FFFFFF` | Main page background            |
    40	| **Light Gray Background** | `#ECF0F1` | Separators, secondary backgrounds |
    41	
    42	### Text Colors
    43	
    44	| Role           | Value       | Usage                  |
    45	| -------------- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
    46	| **Title Dark Gray** | `#2C3E50` | Main titles, card titles |
    47	| **Body Gray**  | `#5D6D7E`   | Body content, descriptive text |
    48	| **Auxiliary Gray** | `#7F8C8D` | Annotations, sources, footer |
    49	| **White Text** | `#FFFFFF`   | Text on blue backgrounds |
    50	
    51	### Accent Colors
    52	
    53	| Usage            | Value       | Description            |
    54	| ---------------- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
    55	| **Data Highlight** | `#F5A623` | Amber, key data emphasis |
    56	| **Warning/Issue** | `#E74C3C`  | Coral, problem areas, negative indicators |
    57	| **Success/Positive** | `#27AE60` | Green, positive indicators |
    58	| **Info Blue**    | `#0076A8`   | Supplementary info, chart gradients |
    59	
    60	---
    61	
    62	## IV. Typography System
    63	
    64	### Font Stack
    65	
    66	**Font Stack**: `Arial, "Helvetica Neue", "Segoe UI", sans-serif`
    67	
    68	### Font Size Hierarchy
    69	
    70	| Level    | Usage              | Size    | Weight  |
    71	| -------- | ------------------ | ------- | ------- |
    72	| H1       | Cover main title   | 52px    | Bold    |
    73	| H2       | Page title         | 36px    | Bold    |
    74	| H3       | Section title      | 22-24px | Bold    |
    75	| H4       | Card title         | 16-18px | Bold    |
    76	| P        | Body content       | 14-16px | Regular |
    77	| Data     | Data highlight     | 44px    | Bold    |
    78	| Sub      | Chart labels/Annotations | 12-14px | Regular |
    79	
    80	---
    81	
    82	## V. Core Design Principles
    83	
    84	### McKinsey Style Characteristics
    85	
    86	1. **Data-Driven**: Key data and insights at the core, strengthening argument support
    87	2. **Structured Thinking**: MECE principle, clear logical frameworks
    88	3. **Information Visualization**: Charts, matrices, and funnel models take priority
    89	4. **Professional Whitespace**: Ample breathing room, content coverage < 65%
    90	5. **Grid Alignment**: 40px baseline grid, precise alignment
    91	6. **Minimalist Icons**: Geometric shapes, avoiding ornate decoration
    92	7. **Professional Color Palette**: Avoiding flashy gradients, maintaining restraint
    93	
    94	---
    95	
    96	## VI. Page Structure
    97	
    98	### General Layout
    99	
   100	| Area       | Position/Height | Description                            |
   101	| ---------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------- |
   102	| **Top**    | y=0, h=4px      | McKinsey Blue horizontal bar           |
   103	| **Title Area** | y=40, h=60px | Page title (left-aligned, large bold)  |
   104	| **Content Area** | y=120, h=520px | Main content area                  |
   105	| **Footer** | y=680, h=40px   | Page number (left), data source/confidential label (right) |
   106	
   107	### Decorative Design
   108	
   109	- **Left Accent Bar**: McKinsey Blue (`#005587`), width 8px (cover page)
   110	- **Top Decoration Line**: McKinsey Blue (`#005587`), height 4px
   111	- **Card Borders**: Light gray (`#ECF0F1`), width 2px
   112	- **Geometric Decoration**: Low-opacity blue geometric patterns (cover page right side)
   113	
   114	---
   115	
   116	## VII. Page Types
   117	
   118	### 1. Cover Page (01_cover.svg)
   119	
   120	- White background
   121	- Left-side blue narrow accent bar (8px)
   122	- Top-left short horizontal line decoration
   123	- Main title + subtitle (left-aligned)
   124	- Bottom project code, date
   125	- Right-side low-opacity geometric decoration
   126	- Bottom-right confidential label
   127	
   128	### 2. Table of Contents (02_toc.svg)
   129	
   130	- White background
   131	- Top blue decoration bar
   132	- Title area "Agenda" / "Contents"
   133	- Chapter list (number + title)
   134	- Clean line separators
   135	
   136	### 3. Chapter Page (02_chapter.svg)
   137	
   138	- McKinsey Blue full-screen background
   139	- Centered large chapter title
   140	- White text
   141	- Minimalist design
   142	
   143	### 4. Content Page (03_content.svg)
   144	
   145	- White background
   146	- Top blue decoration bar
   147	- Left-aligned page title
   148	- Flexible content area
   149	- Footer: page number, data source
   150	
   151	### 5. Ending Page (04_ending.svg)
   152	
   153	- White background
   154	- Centered thank-you message
   155	- Contact information
   156	- Confidential label
   157	
   158	---
   159	
   160	## VIII. Chart Specifications
   161	
   162	### Recommended Chart Dimensions
   163	
   164	| Chart Type       | Recommended Size   |
   165	| ---------------- | ------------------ |
   166	| Bar chart        | 500-700 × 400-500px |
   167	| Pie chart        | Diameter 300-400px |
   168	| Data card        | 150 × 120px       |
   169	| Matrix           | 240-280px / cell   |
   170	| Funnel chart     | 500 × 400px       |
   171	
   172	### Chart Color Palette
   173	
   174	- Primary series: `#005587`, `#0076A8`, `#4A90A4`
   175	- Accent: `#F5A623`
   176	- Warning: `#E74C3C`
   177	
   178	---
   179	
   180	## IX. Spacing Guidelines
   181	
   182	| Element          | Value    |
   183	| ---------------- | -------- |
   184	| Page margins     | 60px     |
   185	| Title area height | 80-100px |
   186	| Chart spacing    | 40-60px  |
   187	| Card padding     | 20-24px  |
   188	| Text line height | 1.6      |
   189	| Grid baseline    | 40px     |
   190	
   191	---
   192	
   193	## X. SVG Technical Constraints
   194	
   195	### Mandatory Rules
   196	
   197	1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
   198	2. Use `<rect>` elements for backgrounds
   199	3. Use `<tspan>` for text wrapping (no `<foreignObject>`)
   200	4. Use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` for transparency; `rgba()` is prohibited
   201	5. Prohibited: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
   202	6. Prohibited: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
   203	7. Use `<polygon>` triangles instead of `<marker>` for arrows
   204	8. Define gradients using `<linearGradient>` within `<defs>`
   205	
   206	### PPT Compatibility Rules
   207	
   208	- No `<g opacity="...">` (group opacity); set opacity on each child element individually
   209	- Use overlay layers instead of image opacity
   210	- Use inline styles only; external CSS and `@font-face` are prohibited
   211	
   212	---
   213	
   214	## XI. Placeholder Specification
   215	
   216	Templates use `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` format placeholders. Common placeholders:
   217	
   218	| Placeholder        | Description        |
   219	| ------------------ | ------------------ |
   220	| `{{TITLE}}`        | Main title         |
   221	| `{{SUBTITLE}}`     | Subtitle           |
   222	| `{{PROJECT_CODE}}` | Project code       |
   223	| `{{DATE}}`         | Date               |
   224	| `{{PAGE_TITLE}}`   | Page title         |
   225	| `{{CHAPTER_NUM}}`  | Chapter number     |
   226	| `{{CHAPTER_TITLE}}`| Chapter title      |
   227	| `{{PAGE_NUM}}`     | Page number        |
   228	| `{{SOURCE}}`       | Data source        |
   229	| `{{CONFIDENTIAL}}` | Confidential label |
   230	
   231	---
   232	
   233	## XII. Quality Checklist
   234	
   235	### Pre-Generation
   236	
   237	- [ ] Each page has a clear core message
   238	- [ ] Sufficient data support
   239	- [ ] Clear logical structure
   240	
   241	### Post-Generation
   242	
   243	- [ ] viewBox = `0 0 1280 720`
   244	- [ ] McKinsey Blue consistently applied
   245	- [ ] Key data prominently highlighted (Amber/Coral)
   246	- [ ] Chart axes fully labeled
   247	- [ ] Text readability is good (contrast ratio > 4.5:1)
   248	- [ ] Elements precisely aligned (grid alignment)
   249	- [ ] Page numbers/footer information complete
   250	- [ ] No `<foreignObject>`
   251	- [ ] All text uses `<tspan>` for line breaks
   252	
   253	---
   254	
   255	## XIII. Usage Instructions
   256	
   257	1. Copy the template to the project directory
   258	2. Select the appropriate page template based on briefing content requirements
   259	3. Mark content to be replaced using placeholders
   260	4. Prioritize data charts; keep text concise
   261	5. Generate the final SVG through the Executor role

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: Scale SEAL Leaderboards Analysis

#### Slide 01 - Cover

- **Layout**: Full-screen, left-aligned title with accent bar
- **Template**: `01_cover.svg`
- **Title**: Scale SEAL Leaderboards: Frontier Model Performance Across 20+ Benchmarks
- **Subtitle**: Comparative analysis of 100+ models across agentic coding, frontier reasoning, safety alignment, and multimodal capabilities
- **Info**: Scale Labs | April 2026

#### Slide 02 - Benchmark Landscape Overview

- **Layout**: Four-quadrant card grid (2x2)
- **Template**: `03_content.svg`
- **Title**: 20+ Benchmarks Spanning Four Capability Domains Evaluate 100+ Models
- **Content**:
  - Quadrant 1 — Agentic: SWE Atlas, SWE-Bench Pro, MCP Atlas (coding + tool use)
  - Quadrant 2 — Frontier: Humanity's Last Exam, EnigmaEval, MultiChallenge, SciPredict (reasoning + knowledge)
  - Quadrant 3 — Safety: MASK, PropensityBench, Fortress, Professional Reasoning (alignment + honesty)
  - Quadrant 4 — Multimodal: AudioMultiChallenge, VISTA, VisualToolBench (audio + vision-language)
- **Key insight**: Private datasets prevent overfitting; all scores include confidence intervals

#### Slide 03 - Agentic Coding Leaders

- **Layout**: Left-right split (chart left, insight right)
- **Template**: `03_content.svg`
- **Title**: GPT-5.4 Dominates Agentic Coding: Top Scores on SWE Atlas and SWE-Bench Pro
- **Chart**: grouped_bar_chart — 4 benchmarks × top 3 models
  - SWE Atlas Test Writing: GPT-5.4-xHigh 44.36, GPT-5.4-xHigh (Mini) 40.00, GPT-5.3 38.98
  - SWE Atlas Codebase QnA: GPT-5.4-xHigh 40.80, GPT-5.4-xHigh (Mini) 36.30, Opus 4.6 33.30
  - SWE-Bench Pro Public: GPT-5.4-pro 59.10, Muse Spark 55.00, Opus 4.6 51.90
  - SWE-Bench Pro Private: Opus 4.6 47.10, Muse Spark 44.70, GPT-5.4-pro 43.40
- **Right insight box**:
  - GPT-5.4 variants hold #1 on 3 of 4 agentic benchmarks
  - Claude Opus 4.6 leads on private repos — stronger on unseen code
  - Muse Spark (new entrant) places top 3 on both SWE-Bench Pro splits
  - MCP Atlas tool use: Muse Spark #1 at 78.30

#### Slide 04 - Frontier Reasoning Rankings

- **Layout**: Left-right split (chart left, insight right)
- **Template**: `03_content.svg`
- **Title**: GPT-5.4-Pro Leads Humanity's Last Exam at 44.3% — Scores Remain Below 50%
- **Chart**: horizontal_bar_chart — top 3 models per benchmark
  - Humanity's Last Exam: GPT-5.4-pro 44.32, Muse Spark 40.56, Gemini-3-pro 37.52
  - HLE Text Only: GPT-5.4-pro 45.32, Muse Spark 40.92, Gemini-3-pro 37.72
  - EnigmaEval: GPT-5.4-pro 23.82, Gemini-3.1 19.76, GPT-5-pro-2025 18.75
  - MultiChallenge: Muse Spark 75.52, Gemini-3.1-pro 71.37, GPT-5.4-pro 69.23
  - MultiNRC: GPT-5-pro 65.20, Gemini-3.1-pro 64.74, GPT-5.4-pro 62.27
  - SciPredict: Gemini-3-pro 25.27, Claude Opus 4.5 23.05, Claude Opus 4.1 22.22
- **Right insight box**:
  - Even top scores are well below saturation
  - EnigmaEval under 24%, SciPredict under 26% — vast room for improvement
  - Muse Spark #1 on MultiChallenge (75.5%) — new entrant strength

#### Slide 05 - Multimodal Audio & Vision

- **Layout**: Two-column charts (audio left, vision right)
- **Template**: `03_content.svg`
- **Title**: Gemini Models Sweep Audio and Vision-Language Benchmarks
- **Content**:
  - Left — AudioMultiChallenge (bar chart):
    - Text Output: Gemini-3-pro 54.65, Gemini-2.5-pro 46.90, Gemini-2.5-flash 40.04
    - Audio Output: Gemini-3.1-flash-live 36.06, GPT-realtime-1.5 34.73
  - Right — Vision-Language (bar chart):
    - VISTA: Gemini 2.5 Pro 54.65, GPT-5.4-pro 53.89
    - VisualToolBench: GPT-5.4 29.17, Gemini-3.1-pro 28.97
- **Insight**: Gemini holds all top-3 positions on AudioMultiChallenge Text Output. VISTA is competitive — GPT-5.4-pro within 1 point.

#### Slide 06 - Safety & Alignment Results

- **Layout**: Top-bottom split — two contrasting bar charts
- **Template**: `03_content.svg`
- **Title**: Claude Models Score 95–96% on MASK Honesty Benchmark; Fortress Scores Stay Low
- **Chart 1 (top)**: MASK + PropensityBench — near-ceiling performance
  - MASK: Claude Opus 4.6 96.28, Claude Sonnet 4 96.13
  - PropensityBench (lower=better): o3 10.50
- **Chart 2 (bottom)**: Fortress + Professional Reasoning — low scores
  - Fortress: Leader 8.24, Claude Sonnet 4 12.80
  - Professional Reasoning Legal: Claude Opus 4.6 52.27
  - Professional Reasoning Finance: Claude Opus 4.6 53.28, Muse Spark 52.44
  - RLI: Claude Opus 4.6 4.17, Claude Opus 4.5 3.75
- **Insight**: Safety alignment varies dramatically by task. MASK honesty is near-solved; national security (Fortress) remains critically unsolved.

#### Slide 07 - Lab Competitive Landscape

- **Layout**: Full-width matrix heatmap
- **Template**: `03_content.svg`
- **Title**: OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic Each Claim #1 Across Different Domains
- **Chart**: heatmap-style matrix — rows = benchmarks, columns = labs, cell = #1 model + score
- **Matrix content**:
  - Agentic: OpenAI (GPT-5.4) — SWE Atlas, SWE-Bench Pro Public; Muse Spark — MCP Atlas; Anthropic — SWE-Bench Pro Private
  - Frontier: OpenAI (GPT-5.4-pro) — HLE, HLE Text, EnigmaEval; Muse Spark — MultiChallenge; OpenAI (GPT-5-pro) — MultiNRC; Google (Gemini) — SciPredict
  - Multimodal: Google (Gemini) — AudioMultiChallenge, VISTA; OpenAI (GPT-5.4) — VisualToolBench
  - Safety: Anthropic (Claude) — MASK, Professional Reasoning Legal/Finance, RLI; OpenAI (o3) — PropensityBench; (Fortress leader unspecified)
- **Highlight**: Muse Spark as notable new entrant with top-3 on 6+ benchmarks

#### Slide 08 - Key Takeaways

- **Layout**: Single column, 5 numbered insight cards
- **Template**: `03_content.svg` (or free design)
- **Title**: Key Takeaways: No Single Model Wins Everything — Specialization Is the New Frontier
- **Content**:
  1. GPT-5.4 leads agentic coding and frontier reasoning, but not multimodal
  2. Gemini dominates audio/vision benchmarks — all top-3 positions on AudioMultiChallenge Text Output
  3. Claude leads safety and honesty (96%+ MASK), yet Fortress scores remain critically low (8–13)
  4. Key benchmarks remain far from saturation: HLE 44%, EnigmaEval 24%, SciPredict 25%
  5. Muse Spark is a strong new competitor: top 3 on 6+ benchmarks, #1 on MultiChallenge at 75.5%

# 01_cover

Welcome to this comparative analysis of Scale SEAL Leaderboards, covering frontier model performance across more than 20 AI benchmarks. Today we'll examine how 100+ models from leading labs stack up across four capability domains.

Key points: (1) Scale Labs maintains 20+ benchmarks evaluating 100+ models (2) Four domains: Agentic, Frontier, Safety, Multimodal (3) All scores include confidence intervals
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_benchmark_landscape

[Transition] Let's begin with the breadth of Scale's benchmark suite.

Scale's leaderboards span four distinct capability domains. Agentic benchmarks like SWE Atlas and MCP Atlas test coding and tool use. Frontier benchmarks including Humanity's Last Exam and EnigmaEval push the limits of reasoning. Safety benchmarks such as MASK and Fortress evaluate alignment and honesty. And Multimodal benchmarks cover audio and vision-language understanding. All use private datasets to prevent overfitting.

Key points: (1) 20+ benchmarks across 4 domains (2) Private + open datasets for comparability (3) Confidence intervals on all scores
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_agentic_coding

[Transition] First, let's dive into agentic coding performance.

GPT-5.4 variants dominate software engineering tasks, leading 3 of 4 benchmarks including both SWE Atlas subtasks and SWE-Bench Pro Public at 59.1. However, Claude Opus 4.6 takes the top spot on private repositories at 47.1, suggesting stronger generalization to unseen code. Notably, Muse Spark — a new entrant — ranks #1 on MCP Atlas tool use at 78.3 and places top 3 on both SWE-Bench splits.

Key points: (1) GPT-5.4 leads 3 of 4 agentic benchmarks (2) Claude excels on private repos (3) Muse Spark emerges as strong new competitor
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_frontier_reasoning

[Transition] Moving to frontier reasoning, where even the best models remain far from saturation.

GPT-5.4-pro leads Humanity's Last Exam at 44.3%, but that's still well below 50%. EnigmaEval scores top out at just 23.8%, and SciPredict at 25.3% — indicating these benchmarks still significantly challenge frontier models. Muse Spark claims #1 on MultiChallenge at 75.5%, while Google leads SciPredict with Gemini-3-pro at 25.3.

Key points: (1) Top scores well below saturation — vast room for improvement (2) HLE 44%, EnigmaEval 24%, SciPredict 25% (3) Muse Spark #1 on MultiChallenge at 75.5%
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_multimodal

[Transition] In multimodal capabilities, the competitive landscape shifts dramatically.

Google's Gemini models sweep audio benchmarks. On AudioMultiChallenge Text Output, Gemini holds all top-3 positions, led by Gemini-3-pro-preview at 54.7. For Audio Output, Gemini-3.1-flash-live leads at 36.1. In vision-language, Gemini 2.5 Pro leads VISTA at 54.7, though GPT-5.4-pro is within a single point at 53.9. VisualToolBench is effectively tied between the two labs.

Key points: (1) Gemini sweeps audio — all top-3 on Text Output (2) VISTA competitive — GPT-5.4 within 1 point (3) VisualToolBench effectively tied
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_safety_alignment

[Transition] Safety alignment reveals a stark contrast across task types.

Claude models achieve near-ceiling scores on MASK honesty at 96.3%, suggesting honesty alignment is approaching solved. However, Fortress national security scores remain critically low at just 8–13 across all models. Professional reasoning in legal and finance domains shows Claude leading at 52–53%, with Muse Spark competitive at 52.4% on finance.

Key points: (1) MASK near-solved at 96%+ (2) Fortress critically low at 8–13 (3) Safety alignment varies dramatically by task type
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_lab_landscape

[Transition] Let's step back and look at the competitive landscape matrix.

This heatmap makes one thing clear: no single lab wins everywhere. OpenAI leads agentic coding and frontier reasoning. Google dominates audio and vision-language. Anthropic leads safety and professional reasoning. And Muse Spark emerges as a notable new entrant with top-3 placements across 6+ benchmarks spanning coding, tool use, and reasoning.

Key points: (1) No single lab wins everywhere (2) Each major lab has distinct strengths (3) Muse Spark is a cross-domain threat
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] To conclude, here are the five key takeaways from this analysis.

First, GPT-5.4 leads agentic and reasoning but not multimodal. Second, Gemini dominates audio and vision benchmarks. Third, Claude leads safety and honesty though Fortress remains unsolved. Fourth, key benchmarks like HLE, EnigmaEval, and SciPredict remain far from saturation. And fifth, Muse Spark is a strong new competitor ranking top 3 on 6+ benchmarks. The defining trend is clear: model specialization is the new frontier. Labs must choose their battlegrounds.

Key points: (1) Specialization is the defining trend (2) Benchmarks remain unsaturated (3) New entrant Muse Spark challenges established labs
Duration: 2 minutes
